title: Frame Budget Scheduler Timeline
description: Once every subsystem runs in one loop, each pass must fit in the 40 ms audio frame. A pass's total is simply the sum of the costs of the tasks that run, and a pass overruns when the total is over 40.0 ms. A cooperative scheduler considers tasks in order of importance and defers any task whose budget no longer fits in what is left of the frame.

learningObjectives: The learner will examine 6 loop passes against the 40 ms frame budget by calculating each pass's total time to within 0.1 ms and deciding whether it overruns, with at least 5 of 6 fully correct.
prerequisites: frame, frame budget, task, task budget, cooperative scheduler, deferral, overrun (all defined in the sections above this block).

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Explore, then fixed-order practice items with one attempt each and immediate explained feedback
keyQuestions: Does a task with a big budget cost its budget?
Can the scheduler interrupt a task that runs too long?
Does turning the scheduler on make every task run?
commonMisconceptions: (1) A task with a big budget only costs its budget. (2) The scheduler can interrupt a task that runs too long. (3) A pass that fits in 40 ms on average cannot overrun. (4) Turning the scheduler on always makes every task run.
assessmentOpportunities: Complete all six passes. Mastery is 5 of 6 fully correct on the first attempt.
